title: Windows PowerShell 5.1 stops a script on any stderr line from a program it runs
observation: With $ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop', Windows PowerShell 5.1 turns each line a native program writes to stderr into a NativeCommandError, and the first one ends the script. Python's unittest runner writes its progress dots to stderr, so scripts/memory.ps1 'test' failed with exit code 1 even though all 27 tests passed when run directly. Setting the preference to 'Continue' around the native call, and letting $LASTEXITCODE decide, fixed it.
recommendation: When a PowerShell wrapper runs a tool that writes progress or warnings to stderr, do not rely on Stop for error handling. Around that call set $ErrorActionPreference to 'Continue' and check $LASTEXITCODE, then restore the old value. Run the tool directly once to tell a real test failure from a wrapper failure.
applies_when: A Windows PowerShell 5.1 script runs Python, Rojo, selene or another program that writes to stderr
A check script exits 1 while the tool it runs reports success
limits: Observed on Windows PowerShell 5.1 with Python 3.12 unittest on one Windows 10 PC; PowerShell 7 treats native stderr differently and was not checked

evidence.detail: scripts/check.ps1 failed at the memory test step with exit code 1 and 27 progress dots on stderr. Running the same unittest directly gave 'Ran 27 tests ... OK'. After the fix in this commit the full check exits 0.
